review_type: result-selected continuation recommendation, not final study acceptance
rationale: Old TC+stock has substantive complete-method value on two important hard roles: it beats TC2 in both U and L on K35 and RB35-T2, and on K35 also beats both inherited BASE and stock. Its K35 path begins exact-close rather than TC2 native-target, with the same own H.

TC2 still provides a valid exact block separation and stronger reoptimized bounds in all five LP domains. Its K20 certificate is faster than old TC but slower than stock; that isolated advantage does not offset the two observed hard-role regressions when selecting the next uniform complete candidate.

The old-TC method has not yet been tested on K15 or RX35-T2. K15 checks preservation of the established fast-proof benefit; RX35-T2 checks the remaining hard-role incumbent/bound tradeoff. These missing facts can change the choice between a uniform old-TC continuation and stopping.

Two added positions complete the same five-role comparison rather than expanding both candidates to eight. This is the permitted landing of the existing TC+stock combination, not a renaming of its gains as TC2 gains.
followup_conditions: Freeze and obtain SHA-bound admission for the two new independent own-H Seed0 positions before running them; keep the same uniform old-TC rule and physical/objective parameters.

After their qualified closeout, choose at most one uniform candidate for any remaining three-role extension. Preservation of K15 proof and a useful or interpretable RX35 endpoint are decision evidence, not a requirement to win every cell.

If the new old-TC positions show important regressions that remove its apparent broader value, report the completed finite negative/mixed comparison and stop expansion. A remaining budget is not a reason to fill a table.
Only request paired Seed1 if uncertainty in a key positive or adverse result could change the adoption/stop decision; do not run it merely because the method remains research-only.
causal_limit: Different AM paths and Native outcomes are observable whole-method changes; one Seed does not identify additive causal runtime or prove a universal dominance rule.
